decisive_question.question: Is the trailing ~3rd-percentile multiple pricing a genuine trough in a self-inflicted, deliberately-reset franchise that re-accelerates as Performance scales and Pace savings land — or does the collapsing forward earnings base (NTM EBITDA 18.5x, FY27 EBIT guided to fall faster than revenue) mean the 'cheap' trailing read is a value trap on a structurally smaller, lower-return business?

evidence_for.claim: Performance grew high single digits on a $16B base with double-digit growth across Running, Football, Tennis and Golf, and much of the revenue decline is deliberate supply cuts (Dunk down ~50%, ~$200M headwind) — a self-inflicted reset, not pure demand loss.

evidence_against.claim: On the forward earnings base the stock is expensive, not cheap: ~29.7x the $1.15–$1.35 FY27 adjusted-EPS guide and NTM TEV/EBITDA 18.46x vs peer median 9.21x.

key_unknowns: Whether the trailing EV/EBITDA at the 3rd own-history percentile (9.6x, median 20.9x) is overshoot or terminal is UNRESOLVED — it is trailing-only with no forward basis and no adjusted-forward figure, so it belongs here, not as a directional point.

No forward-adjusted EV/EBITDA or net-debt/adjusted-EBITDA was derivable ('no revised guidance at the drawdown to read an adjusted figure from') — the forward leverage/valuation picture on management's basis is missing.

No segment EBITDA is disclosed (7 revenue segments, no segment profit split beyond NIKE Brand vs Converse) — the profitability of the declining China/Sportswear/Jordan mix versus growing Performance cannot be isolated; an opacity gap that leans bearish.
The November 16–17 Investor Day 'long-term growth algorithm' is the key catalyst that would confirm or deny the EBIT-margin and Pace-savings path — not yet delivered.

The decisive variable — when (or whether) total revenue inflects positive, given Sportswear+Jordan (~half of revenue) and China are all still falling and guided to bleed into FY28 — is unresolved; management declined to commit to FY28 positivity.
Peer comparability is explicitly flagged HETEROGENEOUS (caps $2.0B–$32.5B vs $55.2B); any read of the discount as earned-vs-residual is confidence-gated and cannot rest on the peer median alone.
The CIQ export date is unverified (a floor ≥ 2026-10-27), so the freshness of the consensus path and revision breadth is a lower bound only.

caveats: NOT A CURRENT SCREEN CANDIDATE — assembled because the name carries an operator follow decision — NIKE, the athletic footwear and apparel company (NIKE, Jordan, Converse), followed as an OVERSHOOT candidate by operator decision 2026-09-22: at $36.10 on 2026-09-21 it is down 51.6% from its 52-week closing high of $74.57 (2025-10-02) and 1.7% above its 52-week low ($35.51, 2026-09-18) — a ~$53.6bn market cap on $46.4bn of FY2026 (May) revenue. The cap band decides where the fund HUNTS, not what it may hold or follow, so absence from it is not a rejection — read the verdict, not the absence: no screen run on file has evaluated it.

business_description.value: NIKE, Inc., together with its subsidiaries, designs, develops, markets, and sells athletic footwear, apparel, equipment, accessories, and services for men, women, and kids in North America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Greater China, the Asia Pacific, and Latin America. The company offers its products under the NIKE, Jordan, Converse, Jumpman, Chuck Taylor, All Star, One Star, Star Chevron, and Jack Purcell trademarks. It also provides a line of performance equipment and accessories, including bags, socks, sport balls, eyewear, timepieces, digital devices, bats, gloves, protective equipment, and other equipment for sports activities; and sports apparel, as well as sells products to wholesale customers and directly to consumers through NIKE Direct operations; distributes and licenses casual sneakers, apparel, and accessories; and markets apparel with licensed college and professional team and league logos. In addition, the company offers consumer services and experiences, including sport focused events and activations; fitness and activity apps; sport, fitness, and wellness content; and digital services and features in retail stores. It sells its products to footwear stores; sporting goods stores; athletic specialty stores; department stores; skate, tennis, and golf shops; and other wholesale accounts through NIKE-owned retail stores, independent distributors, licensees, sales representatives, and digital platforms. The company was formerly known as Blue Ribbon Sports, Inc. and changed its name to NIKE, Inc. in May 1971. NIKE, Inc. was founded in 1964 and is headquartered in Beaverton, Oregon.

historical_forecast_error.eligibility_note: Each observation is the consensus on the eve of the result — lead time ~0 — so it measures last-mile surprise: a cross-check on scenario severity and on how wrong late consensus has been. It is NOT a distribution of how far consensus moves over a holding period; that needs point-in-time consensus snapshots, which no Estimates Report carries. Each 'actual' is the figure CIQ's Estimates set against its own consensus, which is often NOT the line the financial statements report; `accounting_basis` names the filer's accounting STANDARD (US GAAP, IFRS), never the basis of that actual.
historical_forecast_error.usage_note: EBIT- or EBITDA-level shock today: error_per_forecast_revenue × today's revenue consensus. Revenue × margin scenario: the SAME year's Revenue pct_error and ratio_error, kept together. ratio_error alone answers how wrong the margin (or capex-intensity) forecast was, and multiplied by revenue it drops the revenue miss's effect. Exact identity: error_per_forecast_revenue = ratio_error + (actual ÷ actual revenue) × (actual revenue ÷ forecast revenue − 1).
